structure.title: A marriage contested
structure.text: Court opposition separates Imogen from Posthumus and creates opportunities for others to control what they know about each other.

structure.title: Dispersed journeys
structure.text: Court intrigue, travel, and military conflict develop in separate places before their accounts must be brought together.

people.name: Iachimo
people.text: A man who wagers on his ability to discredit her fidelity.

context.title: Evidence at a distance
context.text: Separation makes reports and objects stand in for direct knowledge. A credible detail can be fitted into a false explanation.
context.takeaway: Distinguish a true observation from a true account.

context.title: Romance rather than realism
context.text: Coincidence, disguise, and remarkable survival belong to the play's form. They make recognition and misrecognition central pleasures.
context.takeaway: Follow the relationships through the improbabilities.

notice.why: Portable evidence can acquire meanings its owner never intended.

notice.text: Notice who trusts testimony too quickly.
notice.why: Confidence can express insecurity rather than understanding.

opening: Imogen marries against her father's wishes, trusting a husband whose confidence in her will soon be put to a grotesque test. Another man wagers that he can prove her unfaithful. He does not need to win her affection if he can manufacture evidence convincing enough to send abroad. Shakespeare sets the intimate danger inside a Britain of court plots, disguises, and threatened war. The adventures multiply around a simple injury: someone who claims to love a woman may find a stranger's account of her easier to believe.
